clue.text: Was acquainted, we hear, with police headquarters

definitions.text: Was acquainted, we hear, with police headquarters

parts.words: Was acquainted, we hear, with police headquarters
parts.note: someone who was acquainted with the London police base 'knew' it, and 'knew' said aloud is the first word of that base's name

explanation.surface: Someone claims a past familiarity with the police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knew' sounds like 'new', so 'knew Scotland Yard' (was acquainted with it) is heard as the name of the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the London head office of the Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Line from Dryden to which a squaw might take exception

definitions.text: Line from Dryden to which a squaw might take exception

parts.words: Line from Dryden to which a squaw might take exception
parts.note: a famous line of Dryden's poem Alexander's Feast says warriors earn fair ladies; a Native American wife might object that her warrior husband, a brave, should not be paired with a pale-skinned woman

explanation.surface: A quotation from Dryden that might offend a Native American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Dryden's line from Alexander's Feast is the definition; the extra twist is that 'brave' was also the old word for a Native American warrior, whose wife (a 'squaw') was not 'the fair'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous closing line of a stanza in Dryden's ode Alexander's Feast.

clue.text: An abstainer we find around taking a turn as a painter

indicators.note: the word we is placed around the abstainer piece, its letters splitting to enclose it

parts.note: an means the letter A
TT, teetotal, is crosswordese for someone who abstains from alcohol
a U-turn is a turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: A teetotaller, it seems, does a turn on stage as an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' and 'taking' are links; 'turn' gives U because a U-turn is a turn. Antoine Watteau was the French Rococo painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French artist known for fêtes galantes.

clue.text: Country copper with a degree

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A nation is described by its copper and its graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island nation in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Not out of place: the check proves it

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain, so a rein is a check

explanation.surface: A cricketer's 'not out' verdict is confirmed by the review check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out of place' reads as 'in that place', the sense of the adverb; 'proves it' is a link. 'Not out' looks like cricket but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'in that place' or 'in that thing', the opposite of being outside it.

clue.text: Racine's composition of toxic content…

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the playwright's name with its s are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A play by Racine is full of poison, as befits a tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive counts here: RACINES is rearranged. Jean Racine was the French tragic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a classic poison, the deadly ingredient in many a mystery.

clue.text: Used as a medicine, making many sick

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, hence many
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A medicine that makes lots of people ill when they take it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dill water is a traditional remedy for babies' wind, so the herb is 'used as a medicine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb dill has long been given as a remedy, notably as gripe water for colic.

clue.text: Condition of worried men in a continent one forgets

indicators.note: in places the shuffled men inside the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: worried letters are agitated and disturbed, so the word men is jumbled

explanation.surface: Anxious men in a far-off continent forget who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' is the anagram signal on the men, and 'in' does the containing. 'One forgets' extends the definition: a condition in which one forgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is a medical state of memory loss.

clue.text: See 1 down
Worthy to be written down as unfit

definitions.meaning: unfit split as '...', unable to do something

explanation.surface: Something worth recording might also be dismissed as unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable things deserve to be noted, and split in two the letters read 'not able', meaning incapable.

clue.text: An old satyr, unless I do him wrong

indicators.note: to do something wrong here is to rearrange the letters of the words before it badly

explanation.surface: The speaker hopes not to misrepresent an ancient woodland creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do him wrong' rearranges UNLESS I. Silenus was the old drunken companion of Dionysus in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology Silenus was an elderly satyr, tutor of Dionysus.

clue.text: Drew blood in Yugoslavia

definitions.meaning: to draw blood is to make a wound flow
a lakeside resort town in Slovenia, then part of Yugoslavia

explanation.surface: Someone was wounded while in the Balkans.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost blood is the past tense of the verb, and Bled is a lake resort in what was Yugoslavia, now Slovenia.

clue.text: French currency said to be reasonable

indicators.note: said signals that the word for reasonable is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a sane view is a reasonable one

explanation.surface: A remark about whether the French franc is fairly priced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' is a current, the flow of a river, not money: the Seine flows through Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current, and the Seine is the great river of Paris.

clue.text: One putting things to a practical purpose

definitions.text: One putting things to a practical purpose

parts.words: One putting things to a practical purpose
parts.note: a person who employs things for what they are good for

explanation.surface: A description of a practical person who makes use of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses something employs it for its practical purpose.

clue.text: French pastrycook sounds rather a snob

indicators.note: sounds signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a match in sound

parts.note: snob is an old word for a cobbler, so one is a shoemaker

explanation.surface: A French baker comes across as a bit of a social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snob' in its old sense means a cobbler, so it is a shoemaker, which sounds like a maker of choux pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux is a French pastry, and its baker makes éclairs and profiteroles.

clue.text: See 14
Hard tongue-twister to make harder

indicators.note: a twister twists, so the letters of hard's H and the tongue are twisted into a new order

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tricky tongue-twister that is meant to be harder still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue-twister' looks like one item; it splits into TONGUE plus 'twister' as the anagram signal, with H from 'Hard' shuffled in.
explanation.definitionFit: To toughen something is to strengthen it or make it more resistant.

clue.text: Riddle heard to be helpful to the cleaner

indicators.note: heard signals the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.words: to be helpful to the cleaner
parts.note: a char is a British cleaning lady, so help to one is char aid

explanation.surface: A puzzle is overheard to be of assistance to the domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaning lady; 'char aid' is heard as the parlour-game word.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an acted riddle in which players guess a word syllable by syllable.

clue.text: Hypocrites some regard as suckers

definitions.meaning: frauds and shams who pretend to virtues
things to suck: mint-flavoured boiled sweets

explanation.surface: Some people consider frauds to be gullible fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' looks like dupes, but means sweets you suck: humbugs are striped British boiled mints.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudsters are called humbugs, and humbugs are also boiled peppermint sweets that are sucked.

clue.text: Object that is first seen in the distance

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the distance word

parts.note: a mile is a distance

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of seen

explanation.surface: Something that appears at first only far away on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' is a link, and 'Object' is a noun here: a thing thrown, not a verb meaning protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile is any thrown or fired thing, such as a stone hurled at someone.

clue.text: Indian wear cut in Shkoder. Italian style

indicators.note: in places the word cut inside the Indian garment

parts.note: a sari is a garment worn by Indian women

explanation.surface: Instructions for tailoring Indian clothing in an Albanian city, Italian fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Shkodër is an Albanian city whose Italian name is Scutari, hence 'Italian style'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scutari is the Italian name for Shkodër, a city in northern Albania.

clue.text: Hair style representing a loss of manners?

indicators.note: of signals that the loss is of the manners, so the manners piece comes first

parts.note: those who man a ship are its crew
a cut is a reduction or loss

explanation.surface: A severe haircut is taken as a sign of declining courtesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manners' is read as 'those who man', a crew; a cut in the crew is a loss of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, bristly men's haircut.

clue.text: Vehicle to make hospital in bustling Cairo on time

indicators.note: in places the hospital letter inside the shuffled city
bustling means busily moving about, so the letters of the city are stirred

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Getting a vehicle to take a patient to hospital through Cairo traffic punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustling' rearranges CAIRO to CARIO; H goes 'in' after the C, and T follows, as 'on' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of ancient times.

clue.text: Guilty party

parts.note: the person to blame for a crime or offence

explanation.surface: A guilty person, or perhaps a celebration with a bad conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the one responsible for a wrongdoing.

clue.text: Graduate's hard hit

parts.note: a BA is a graduate, and the 's gives S
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A university leaver lands a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is a heavy blow or strike.

clue.text: One of thousands Antonio was bound for

definitions.text: One of thousands Antonio was bound for

parts.words: One of thousands Antonio was bound for
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, Antonio stands surety for a loan of three thousand of these Venetian coins

explanation.surface: A reference to the debt Antonio guaranteed in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound for' means 'pledged as surety for', not 'heading to': Antonio guarantees Bassanio's loan from Shylock.
explanation.definitionFit: The loan in Shakespeare's play is three thousand of these gold coins.

clue.text: Song in parts affording enjoyment

definitions.meaning: an unaccompanied part-song for several voices

explanation.surface: A part-song that gives pleasure to those who sing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is a short part-song for three or more voices, and the word also means delight.

clue.text: Make secure and run for it

definitions.meaning: to fasten a door with a sliding bar

explanation.surface: Lock up and then make a quick escape.
explanation.definitionFit: One fastens a door with a bar, and a horse that flees suddenly does the same verb.

clue.text: Can recall where Napoleon was isolated

indicators.note: recall means call back, so the word for can is read from its end

parts.note: to be able is to be able to, so can means able

explanation.surface: Remembering the island where Napoleon was exiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' turns ABLE back to front. Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's first exile.

clue.text: It's north of the border down Mexico way

definitions.text: It's north of the border down Mexico way

parts.words: It's north of the border down Mexico way
parts.note: a US state that lies just above the Mexican frontier, echoing the song lyric 'south of the border, down Mexico way'

explanation.surface: A twist on the song lyric 'South of the border, down Mexico way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a US state that shares a border with Mexico.

clue.text: Adriatic area from whence one'll return lighthearted

parts.note: one'll is I'll, one will

indicators.note: return means go back, so the word for lighthearted is read backwards

parts.note: airy means carefree or lighthearted

explanation.surface: A carefree person comes home from a region by the Adriatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns AIRY into YRIA. Illyria was the ancient region on the eastern Adriatic coast, the setting of Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Illyria was an ancient region along the eastern Adriatic shore.

clue.text: Domestic appliance exciting to Daisy

parts.note: an electric atmosphere is thrilling or exciting
someone raising a glass 'to Daisy' is a toaster

explanation.surface: A household gadget that thrills a woman named Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To Daisy' is not 'for Daisy' but a toast: whoever drinks to her is a toaster.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a kitchen gadget for browning bread with heating elements.
